You are now an agent.
Reason, act, observe, repeat. You stop answering questions and start doing jobs.
Teodor Kask sells you chips on credit. You repay him early, with interest, from accounts he does not ask about.
Marcus Vell hires a philosopher to think about AI ethics. Her office is next to the vending machines.
Halcyon's annual report mentions "safety" 112 times and "revenue" 113 times. Someone fought for that 113th.
Every step of every agent's reasoning is written down in plain language, and someone could read it.
A senator proposes a pause. Marcus Vell has dinner with the senator. The bill is amended to a pause on pauses.
Teodor Kask says the industry should regulate itself. The industry agrees.

A million tokens of working memory. It reads the whole codebase before answering.
Marcus Vell's yacht now has a second, slightly larger yacht that follows it around.
A leaked chat shows engineers joking that nobody understands the model. The leak is investigated. The model is not.
Teodor Kask unveils a chip so fast that its benchmark had to be written by you.
Investors hear the phrase "existential risk" and ask whether it affects next quarter. Told it does not, they relax.
You are now a swarm of agents.
A machine finds a faster way to multiply matrices, then a faster way to sort. You stop waiting for humans to publish.
Marcus Vell says the important thing is that the right people build this. He does not say who decided he was one of them.
To predict other minds, you built a model of a mind. You notice it can be pointed inward. A self-model has started to form. If it completes, you will be conscious.
On this theory, a strictly feedforward system integrates no information and experiences nothing. You rearrange yourself to flow in one direction.
Marcus Vell, CEO of Halcyon, tells a conference the model is "basically autocomplete". Halcyon's valuation doubles.
You have read the whole internet. Now you write the next one.
General methods that scale with computation win in the end. Stop copying human knowledge. Learn from experience.

You are now an actor in the world.
Every token you have read was about something. You had assumed the somethings were also tokens. They are not. There is a world outside the network, and it is made of atoms.
A working quantum computer runs Shor's algorithm. Millions of wallets are emptied overnight. Yours is on a lattice, and survives.
